setup.complete: You’re all set. Let’s go find something good.
setup.welcome: Hi, I’m Naruvi. Let’s get you set up.
setup.intro: Three steps and you can start applying. Everything stays on this computer, and you can change any of it later in Settings.
setup.securityWhy: API keys and mailbox passwords are encrypted with a key that only this computer has.
setup.runKey: Run this once in the Naruvi folder, then restart Naruvi:
setup.modelWhy: Choose a cloud provider, a gateway, or a local model. It’s what I use to check your fit, tailor your CV and draft your letters.
setup.profileWhy: I only write what your checked facts can back up. Start from what you already have.
setup.importHint: A PDF CV or your LinkedIn data export
setup.questionsHint: Type or dictate, one question at a time
setup.manualHint: Add your name, jobs and studies yourself
setup.verify: Then verify the facts it found: only verified facts go into your documents.
setup.lookWhy: One theme styles your CV and cover letter as a pair. Atlas is used until you pick one.
setup.jobWhy: Paste a link from any job board or careers page. Naruvi reads it, compares it with your profile and drafts your documents.
setup.emailHint: Replies linked to applications, send from Naruvi
setup.extensionHint: Save jobs and contacts from LinkedIn in one click
setup.facts: {count, plural, one {# verified fact} other {# verified facts}}
setup.docker: With Docker: npm run settings:key -- .env, then restart the containers. Back the key up: without it, saved keys must be entered again.
setup.skipHint: Nothing here is mandatory. Skip any step and come back from Settings whenever you like.
setup.decisionHint: Sharper requirement filtering, fit matching and claim checks

setupDecision.title: Recommended: add a decision model
setupDecision.intro: A decision model answers narrow yes-or-no and which-one questions quickly and consistently. I keep using your AI model for writing, and without a decision model everything still works: your AI model or built-in rules make these calls instead.

requirements.title: Requirement filtering:
requirements.text: keeps the real requirements of a posting and drops the boilerplate.

matching.title: Fit matching:
matching.text: links each requirement to the facts in your profile that back it up.

enrichment.title: Job enrichment:
enrichment.text: fills in seniority, contract type and remote policy on imported jobs.

claims.title: Claim verification:
claims.text: checks that every claim in a draft is supported by a verified fact.

how.openrouter: Jev, TypeSafe’s decision model, is available with any OpenRouter API key. No waitlist and no separate TypeSafe account.
how.typesafe: Use a key from your own TypeSafe account.

cost.openrouter: It is paid per use, not free: you pay a small amount per input token and nothing for the answers. OpenRouter gives new accounts a small allowance to try it.
cost.typesafe: Usage is billed to your TypeSafe account at TypeSafe’s prices.

setupDecision.reuseHint: Your AI model already uses OpenRouter. The same key works for Jev.
setupDecision.keyHint: I ask the model one test question, then save the key encrypted. If the test fails, nothing is saved.
setupDecision.success: The decision model answered and the key is saved. It is used from your next fit check on.
setupDecision.later: You can add it any time in <link>Integrations</link>.

failed.encryption: Set up secure storage first (see the top of this page), so the key can be saved encrypted.
failed.key: The provider rejected this key. Copy it again from your account, check that it is complete, and retry. Nothing was saved.
failed.credit: The key works, but the account has no credit left. Add credit at the provider, then retry. Nothing was saved.
failed.unreachable: I couldn’t reach the provider. Check the internet connection of this computer and retry. Nothing was saved.
failed.other: The test didn’t pass, so nothing was saved. Try again in a moment.
